name: IR Module
purpose: Finds objects close in front of it
summary: IR LED and photodiode pair that pulls its output LOW when an object is 2–30 cm in front of it.
tip: Turn the blue trimmer to set the range. The output is active LOW (LOW = object present).

projects.title: Obstacle buzzer
projects.description: Beep a buzzer and light an LED whenever something comes close.

projects.title: Visitor counter
projects.description: Count people passing a doorway and show the total on a 16x2 I2C LCD.

projects.title: Obstacle-avoiding robot
projects.description: Two IR modules on a 2WD chassis steer the robot away from walls.

name: Flame Sensor
summary: IR photodiode tuned to 760–1100 nm that detects the light of a flame up to about 80 cm away.
tip: Sunlight and incandescent bulbs also trigger it, so test indoors. On most boards the output goes LOW when a flame is seen.

projects.title: Flame alert
projects.description: Sound a buzzer and flash a red LED when a candle flame is detected.

projects.title: Stove watch
projects.description: Alert if the stove flame goes out while a gas sensor still detects LPG.

projects.title: Fire-fighting robot
projects.description: Three flame sensors locate the flame and a small pump or fan puts it out.

name: TSOP Obstacle Sensor
purpose: Finds obstacles, even in bright light
summary: Obstacle sensor that uses a modulated 38 kHz IR beam and a TSOP receiver, so it ignores ambient light far better than a plain IR module.
tip: Modulation makes it stable in bright rooms. Adjust the trimmer for range and check the onboard LED.

projects.title: Sunlight-proof door chime
projects.description: Play a short tune when someone walks past, even near a window.

projects.title: Shop entry counter
projects.description: Count customers and store the daily total in EEPROM so it survives power loss.

projects.title: Maze-solving robot
projects.description: Front and side TSOP sensors let a robot follow the left wall through a maze.

name: IR Remote Module
purpose: Lets you control things with a remote
summary: Kit with a 17-key NEC IR remote and a 38 kHz receiver module that decodes the button presses.
tip: Install the IRremote library and print the received command codes first, then map each key.

projects.title: Remote LED
projects.description: Turn LEDs on and off with keys 1–3 on the remote.

projects.title: 4-channel remote switch board
projects.description: Toggle four relays (lights, fan) from the remote, with an all-off key.

projects.title: IR-controlled robot car
projects.description: Drive a robot with the arrow keys and set its speed with the number keys.

name: LDR Module
purpose: Tells if it is day or night
summary: Light-dependent resistor with a comparator that switches its output when the light crosses a threshold you set.
tip: On most boards DO goes HIGH in the dark. Use the bare 12 mm LDR if you need an analog light level.

projects.title: Automatic night light
projects.description: Switch an LED on when the room gets dark.

projects.title: Smart street-light model
projects.description: Lamps turn on at dusk and only go bright when an IR sensor sees a car.

projects.title: Sun-tracking curtain
projects.description: A servo opens the curtain at sunrise and closes it at night, with manual override.

name: TSOP Remote Receiver
purpose: Reads buttons from a TV remote
summary: TSOP1838 38 kHz IR receiver on a small breakout with a status LED, for decoding TV and AC remotes.
tip: Works with almost any household remote. Print the raw protocol and command to identify keys.

projects.title: Remote code reader
projects.description: Print the protocol and key code of every remote in your home.

projects.title: TV-remote volume knob
projects.description: Use your TV remote to control the brightness of an LED strip.

projects.title: IR remote cloner
projects.description: Record codes from one remote and replay them with an IR LED.

name: TCRT5000 Line Sensor
purpose: Tells black lines from white surfaces
summary: Reflective IR sensor that tells black from white surfaces 1–8 mm away, with digital and analog outputs.
tip: Black surfaces reflect little IR, so DO usually goes HIGH over a black line. Mount it 3–5 mm above the floor.

projects.title: Black/white detector
projects.description: Light an LED when the sensor is over black tape.

projects.title: Two-sensor line follower
projects.description: Two TCRT5000 sensors keep a robot on a black tape track.

projects.title: Tachometer
projects.description: Count a white mark on a spinning shaft and show RPM on an LCD.

name: IR 5 Array
purpose: Shows where a line is under a robot
summary: Five TCRT5000 sensors on one bar that report the line's position under the robot.
tip: A0–A5 also work as digital pins. Weight the channels −2…+2 to get a line-position error for PID.

projects.title: Line position display
projects.description: Show which of the five sensors sees the line using five LEDs.

projects.title: Junction-counting robot
projects.description: Follow a line and stop at the third crossing, like a delivery robot.

projects.title: PID line follower
projects.description: Tune Kp, Ki and Kd for a fast, smooth line follower with wheel encoders.

name: Laser Receiver
purpose: Knows when a laser beam hits it
summary: Receiver tuned for a laser spot; its output goes HIGH while the laser beam hits the sensor.
tip: Pair it with the 650 nm laser module. Shield the sensor from room light with a short tube.

projects.title: Laser tripwire
projects.description: Sound a buzzer when someone breaks the laser beam.

projects.title: Race timer
projects.description: Two laser gates measure the time a toy car takes between them.

projects.title: Laser security grid
projects.description: Mirrors bounce one beam across a doorway, with arm/disarm by keypad.

name: Eye Blink Sensor
summary: IR sensor mounted on a glasses frame that detects when the eyelid closes.
tip: Keep the IR LED about 1 cm from the eye. Never use laser modules near the eyes.

projects.title: Blink counter
projects.description: Count blinks per minute and print them to the Serial Monitor.

projects.title: Drowsiness alarm
projects.description: Buzz if the eye stays closed for more than 1.5 seconds.

projects.title: Blink-to-talk aid
projects.description: Blink patterns pick phrases on an LCD for people who cannot speak.

name: Ultrasonic Sensor HC-SR04
summary: Measures distance from 2 to 400 cm by timing an ultrasonic echo.
tip: Send a 10 µs pulse on Trig, then distance in cm = echo time (µs) ÷ 58. Soft surfaces absorb sound and give poor readings.

projects.title: Digital ruler
projects.description: Print distance in cm to the Serial Monitor.

projects.title: Smart dustbin
projects.description: The lid opens with a servo when a hand comes within 20 cm.

projects.title: Ultrasonic radar
projects.description: Sweep the sensor on a servo and draw a radar map in Processing.

name: Ultrasonic Waterproof (JSN-SR04T)
summary: Waterproof ultrasonic probe on a cable, measuring 25–450 cm in wet or dirty places.
tip: Its blind zone is about 25 cm, so mount it at least that far above the full water level.

projects.title: Water depth meter
projects.description: Print the water depth below the probe to the Serial Monitor.

projects.title: Tank level indicator
projects.description: Show tank % on an LCD and beep when it is nearly full.

projects.title: Automatic pump controller
projects.description: Run the motor at 20% level and stop at 95%, with dry-run protection.

name: Rain Sensor
summary: Rain plate with a comparator board; the more water on the plate, the lower the analog reading.
tip: Power the module from a digital pin only while reading, to slow corrosion of the plate.

projects.title: Rain alarm
projects.description: Beep when the first raindrops fall on the plate.

projects.title: Rain intensity meter
projects.description: Show dry, drizzle or heavy rain with three LEDs.

projects.title: Auto clothes-line cover
projects.description: A motor pulls a cover over drying clothes when it starts raining.

name: Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor
purpose: Checks if the soil is wet or dry
summary: Corrosion-resistant soil moisture probe that measures capacitance instead of passing current through the soil.
tip: Record the reading in dry air and in water to calibrate. A lower reading means wetter soil. Keep the electronics at the top dry.

projects.title: Plant mood light
projects.description: Green, yellow or red LED shows how thirsty your plant is.

projects.title: Automatic plant watering
projects.description: A relay runs a mini pump when moisture falls below 35%.

projects.title: Multi-pot irrigation system
projects.description: Four probes and four valves water each pot on its own schedule.

name: Soil Moisture Sensor
purpose: Checks if the soil needs water
summary: Resistive two-prong soil probe with a comparator board; low-cost and easy to start with.
tip: The prongs corrode within weeks if powered all the time. Switch power from a digital pin and read every few minutes.

projects.title: Thirsty plant buzzer
projects.description: Chirp once an hour when the soil is dry.

projects.title: Soil moisture bar graph
projects.description: Show moisture as a 5-LED bar graph.

projects.title: Garden watering scheduler
projects.description: Water only in the morning, and only if the soil is dry and it isn't raining.

name: Water Level Sensor
purpose: Detects water and how high it is
summary: PCB with exposed parallel traces whose analog output rises as more of it is covered by water.
tip: Not linear and it corrodes over time. Power it only while reading and use it for 'low/half/full' levels.

projects.title: Leak detector
projects.description: Beep if water is detected on the floor under a washing machine.

projects.title: Pet bowl monitor
projects.description: Blink an LED when the water bowl runs low.

projects.title: Hydroponic reservoir manager
projects.description: Top up the reservoir with a pump and log the level and refill times.

name: DHT11
summary: Basic temperature (0–50 °C, ±2 °C) and humidity (20–90 %, ±5 %) sensor on a single data pin.
tip: Read at most once per second. If you get NaN, check the wiring and that you chose DHT11 in the code.

projects.title: Room thermometer
projects.description: Print temperature and humidity every 2 seconds.

projects.title: Auto fan
projects.description: Turn a fan on through a relay above 30 °C.

projects.title: Mini climate logger
projects.description: Log temperature and humidity to an SD card every minute for a week.

name: DHT22
summary: Accurate temperature (−40–80 °C, ±0.5 °C) and humidity (0–100 %, ±2 %) sensor, an upgrade from the DHT11.
tip: Wait at least 2 seconds between reads. Bare sensors need a 10 kΩ pull-up on DATA; modules usually include it.

projects.title: Comfort index
projects.description: Compute and print the heat index from temperature and humidity.

projects.title: Weather station
projects.description: Show temperature, humidity and pressure on an LCD with a BMP280.

projects.title: Egg incubator controller
projects.description: Hold 37.5 °C with a heater and 55 % humidity, with turn reminders.

name: PIR Sensor (HC-SR501)
summary: Passive infrared sensor that detects people moving up to about 7 m away.
tip: Give it about 60 seconds to settle after power-up. Two trimmers set the sensitivity and how long the output stays on.

projects.title: Motion light
projects.description: Turn an LED on for 10 seconds when someone walks in.

projects.title: Room occupancy counter
projects.description: Log motion events per hour to find when a room is used.

projects.title: Dual-tech intruder alarm
projects.description: Raise the alarm only when both the PIR and a microwave radar trigger.

name: TTP223B Touch
purpose: A button that works by touch
summary: Capacitive touch pad whose output goes HIGH while it is touched; it works through thin plastic or glass.
tip: Solder pad A to make it a toggle, or pad B to make the output active LOW.

projects.title: Touch lamp
projects.description: Each touch toggles an LED on or off.

projects.title: Touch dimmer
projects.description: A short tap toggles the light and holding it fades the brightness.

projects.title: Hidden touch lock
projects.description: Tap a secret rhythm on a hidden pad to open a servo lock.

name: Sound Sensor (3-pin)
purpose: Detects loud sounds like a clap
summary: Microphone with a comparator that gives a digital pulse when the sound is louder than the threshold you set.
tip: Turn the trimmer until the LED just goes off in a quiet room. Some boards output LOW on sound, others HIGH.

projects.title: Clap LED
projects.description: Each clap toggles an LED.

projects.title: Double-clap switch
projects.description: Two claps within a second toggle a relay-controlled lamp.

projects.title: Classroom noise meter
projects.description: Count loud events per minute and show green/amber/red lights.

name: Sound Sensor (4-pin)
purpose: Measures how loud a sound is
summary: Microphone module with both a threshold output and an analog output that follows the sound level.
tip: The AO signal is small. Sample quickly and use the peak-to-peak value over 50 ms as the sound level.

projects.title: Sound level plot
projects.description: Plot the sound level in the Arduino Serial Plotter.

projects.title: Music VU meter
projects.description: An 8-LED bar graph dances to the music.

projects.title: Clap-pattern lock
projects.description: Unlock a servo latch only after a secret clap rhythm.

name: HC-89 Slot Interrupt Sensor
purpose: Counts things passing through a slot
summary: Slotted optocoupler that changes its output whenever something passes through the slot.
tip: Use D2 or D3 with attachInterrupt() so no pulses are missed at high speed.

projects.title: Slot counter
projects.description: Count how many cards you push through the slot.

projects.title: Fan RPM meter
projects.description: Measure the RPM of a fan blade passing through the slot.

projects.title: Closed-loop motor speed
projects.description: Hold a DC motor at a set RPM with PID control and PWM.

name: Motor Encoder (LM393)
purpose: Measures how fast a wheel turns
summary: Slot speed sensor with an LM393 comparator, made for 20-slot encoder discs on robot wheels.
tip: With a 20-slot disc, RPM = pulses per second × 3. Use an interrupt pin (D2/D3).

projects.title: Wheel RPM
projects.description: Print wheel RPM once a second.

projects.title: Drive straight
projects.description: Match two wheel speeds so a robot drives in a straight line.

projects.title: Odometry robot
projects.description: Drive an exact square by counting encoder ticks for each side and turn.

name: MQ2 Smoke Sensor
summary: Gas sensor module for smoke, LPG, propane and hydrogen (about 300–10000 ppm).
tip: The heater draws about 150 mA, so give it 24 hours to burn in when new and 1–2 minutes to warm up each time. Readings drift, so compare against a clean-air baseline.

projects.title: Smoke alarm
projects.description: Buzz when the reading jumps above the clean-air baseline.

projects.title: Kitchen safety alarm
projects.description: Combine smoke and flame detection and turn on an exhaust fan.

projects.title: Gas alarm with SMS alert
projects.description: Send an SMS through a GSM module when smoke is detected.

name: MQ3 Alcohol Sensor
summary: Gas sensor module for alcohol vapour, used in breathalyser demos.
tip: The heater draws about 150 mA, so give it 24 hours to burn in when new and 1–2 minutes to warm up each time. Readings drift, so compare against a clean-air baseline. This is a demo device, not a legal breath-alcohol tester.

projects.title: Alcohol detector
projects.description: Light an LED when alcohol vapour is near (try hand sanitiser).

projects.title: Breathalyser level meter
projects.description: Show a 0–10 level on an LCD after a 5-second blow.

projects.title: Vehicle ignition interlock model
projects.description: A relay blocks a toy car's motor when alcohol is detected.

name: MQ4 Methane Sensor
summary: Gas sensor module for methane (CNG / natural gas) from about 200 to 10000 ppm.
tip: The heater draws about 150 mA, so give it 24 hours to burn in when new and 1–2 minutes to warm up each time. Readings drift, so compare against a clean-air baseline.

projects.title: Methane leak indicator
projects.description: LED and buzzer warn when methane is detected.

projects.title: Biogas level monitor
projects.description: Track gas concentration in a biogas digester over the day.

projects.title: Auto gas shut-off
projects.description: Close a solenoid valve and start an exhaust fan on a methane leak.

name: MQ6 LPG Sensor
summary: Gas sensor module for LPG, butane and propane, the gases in Indian cooking cylinders.
tip: The heater draws about 150 mA, so give it 24 hours to burn in when new and 1–2 minutes to warm up each time. Readings drift, so compare against a clean-air baseline.

projects.title: LPG leak alarm
projects.description: Loud beeps and a red LED when LPG is detected.

projects.title: Gas leak detector with fan
projects.description: Start an exhaust fan through a relay until the gas level drops.

projects.title: Cylinder safety system
projects.description: Close the cylinder valve with a servo and send a GSM alert.

name: MQ7 Carbon Monoxide Sensor
summary: Gas sensor module for carbon monoxide (about 20–2000 ppm).
tip: For accurate CO readings the heater must cycle between 5V for 60 s and 1.4V for 90 s. Running it at a constant 5V only shows trends. Never rely on it as a life-safety alarm.

projects.title: CO trend plot
projects.description: Plot the CO reading in the Serial Plotter near a candle.

projects.title: CO warning light
projects.description: Amber and red LEDs show rising CO levels with a buzzer.

projects.title: Heater-cycled CO meter
projects.description: Drive the heater with a MOSFET PWM cycle for proper CO measurement.

name: MQ135 Air Quality Sensor
purpose: Checks if the air is clean
summary: General air-quality sensor that responds to NH3, NOx, benzene, smoke and CO2.
tip: The heater draws about 150 mA, so give it 24 hours to burn in when new and 1–2 minutes to warm up each time. Readings drift, so compare against a clean-air baseline. Use it for relative air-quality levels, not exact CO2 ppm.

projects.title: Air quality traffic light
projects.description: Green, amber or red LED for good, moderate or poor air.

projects.title: Ventilation controller
projects.description: Run a fan when air quality is poor and stop it when it recovers.

projects.title: Air quality logger
projects.description: Log MQ135, dust and DHT22 readings to an SD card as CSV.

name: Tilt Sensor (SW-520D)
summary: Ball switch that opens or closes when the module tilts past about 45°.
tip: It's a mechanical ball, so debounce it in code by ignoring changes for 50 ms.

projects.title: Tilt alarm
projects.description: Beep when a box is tipped over.

projects.title: Digital hourglass
projects.description: Flip the device over to restart an LED timer.

projects.title: Bike anti-theft alarm
projects.description: Arm with an RFID tag and sound a siren if the bike is moved.

name: Vibration Sensor (SW-420)
summary: Spring vibration switch with a comparator that outputs a pulse when the module is shaken or knocked.
tip: Count pulses over a short window to measure how strong the vibration is.

projects.title: Knock alarm
projects.description: Buzz when someone knocks on a door.

projects.title: Washing machine done alert
projects.description: Notify when vibration stops for two minutes.

projects.title: Seismograph
projects.description: Plot vibration intensity over time and log events to SD.

name: Inductive Proximity Sensor (NPN)
summary: Industrial LJ12A3-4-Z/BX sensor that detects metal up to 4 mm away without touching it.
tip: It needs 6–36V, so use a 12V supply and connect its ground to the Nano. The NPN output only pulls LOW, so INPUT_PULLUP keeps the Nano pin at a safe 5V.

projects.title: Metal detector LED
projects.description: Light an LED when a screw is near the sensor face.

projects.title: Can counter
projects.description: Count metal cans on a conveyor and show the total.

projects.title: Metal/plastic sorter
projects.description: A servo pushes metal parts off a conveyor into a separate bin.

name: TSL2561 Lux Sensor
purpose: Measures exactly how bright the light is
summary: Digital light sensor with separate visible and infrared channels that reports real lux values.
tip: I2C address 0x39 by default. Many breakouts are 3.3V only, so power it from 3.3V.

projects.title: Lux meter
projects.description: Print lux readings every second.

projects.title: Auto-brightness lamp
projects.description: An LED dims or brightens to keep the desk light steady.

projects.title: Photography light meter
projects.description: Calculate shutter speed for a chosen ISO and aperture, shown on an LCD.

name: GY-21 HTU21
purpose: Measures temperature and humidity very precisely
summary: Precise I2C temperature (±0.3 °C) and humidity (±2 %) sensor.
tip: Address 0x40. The GY-21 board has a regulator and level shifting, so 5V is fine.

projects.title: Precise thermometer
projects.description: Print temperature and humidity with two decimals.

projects.title: Dew-point alert
projects.description: Warn when the surface temperature nears the dew point (risk of mould).

projects.title: Humidity-controlled cabinet
projects.description: Run a dehumidifier fan to keep camera lenses below 45 % RH.

name: HMC5883L Compass
summary: Three-axis magnetometer used as a digital compass.
tip: Run an I2C scanner first. Address 0x1E means HMC5883L, while 0x0D means the board has the QMC5883L clone chip and needs the QMC5883LCompass library.

projects.title: Compass heading
projects.description: Print the heading in degrees.

projects.title: Compass needle
projects.description: A servo always points north.

projects.title: Heading-hold robot
projects.description: Drive a robot on a fixed compass heading, correcting drift with PID.

name: BH1750 Light Sensor
summary: Digital ambient-light sensor that reads 1–65535 lux directly, with no calibration needed.
tip: Address 0x23 (ADDR low) or 0x5C (ADDR high). Simpler and cheaper than the TSL2561.

projects.title: Lux meter
projects.description: Print the light level in lux every second.

projects.title: Smart study lamp
projects.description: Fade an LED lamp to keep 500 lux on your desk.

projects.title: Grow-light controller
projects.description: Top up daylight with grow lights to reach a daily light target.

name: ADXL345 Accelerometer
summary: Three-axis accelerometer (±2 to ±16 g) with built-in tap and free-fall detection.
tip: Address 0x53 with SDO to GND. In full-resolution mode each count is about 3.9 mg.

projects.title: Tilt angles
projects.description: Print pitch and roll in degrees.

projects.title: Digital spirit level
projects.description: Five LEDs show when a surface is level.

projects.title: Wearable fall detector
projects.description: Detect free-fall, impact and then stillness, and sound an alarm.

name: MPU6050 Gyro + Accelerometer
summary: Six-axis motion sensor with a 3-axis gyroscope and a 3-axis accelerometer.
tip: Address 0x68 (AD0 low). Combine the gyro and accelerometer with a complementary filter for steady angles.

projects.title: Angle meter
projects.description: Print pitch and roll angles in the Serial Plotter.

projects.title: Gesture-controlled car
projects.description: Tilt your hand to drive a robot car.

projects.title: Self-balancing robot
projects.description: Balance a two-wheel robot with a PID loop.

name: MAX30100 Pulse Oximeter
purpose: Measures heart rate and oxygen level
summary: Optical heart-rate and SpO2 sensor that you read with a fingertip on the window.
tip: Address 0x57. Many green boards have I2C pull-ups to 1.8V that stop it working with a Nano. If it isn't detected, remove the three 4.7 kΩ resistors and add pull-ups to 3.3V.

projects.title: Finger detector
projects.description: Print the IR value and detect when a finger is placed.

projects.title: Heart-rate display
projects.description: Show BPM on an LCD with a beat LED.

projects.title: Pulse oximeter
projects.description: Show BPM and SpO2, with an alarm when SpO2 drops below 92 %.

name: MAX30102 Pulse Oximeter
purpose: Measures heart rate and oxygen better
summary: Improved heart-rate and SpO2 sensor with a larger FIFO and lower noise than the MAX30100.
tip: Address 0x57. Keep your finger still with light pressure, because movement ruins the reading.

projects.title: Beat plotter
projects.description: Plot the raw IR signal and watch your heartbeat.

projects.title: Finger heart-rate monitor
projects.description: Average BPM over 4 beats and show it on an LCD.

projects.title: Health band logger
projects.description: Log BPM with timestamps and flag readings outside 50–120 BPM.

name: BMP180 Pressure Sensor
summary: Barometric pressure (300–1100 hPa) and temperature sensor; it can estimate altitude.
tip: Address 0x77. For a true altitude, set your local sea-level pressure.

projects.title: Barometer
projects.description: Print pressure in hPa and temperature.

projects.title: Weather trend predictor
projects.description: Predict 'sunny' or 'rain likely' from the 3-hour pressure trend.

projects.title: Model-rocket altimeter
projects.description: Record the peak altitude and store it in EEPROM.

name: BMP280 Pressure Sensor
purpose: Measures air pressure and height accurately
summary: Newer, more precise barometric pressure and temperature sensor (±1 hPa).
tip: The purple 6-pin GY-BMP280 board is 3.3V only, so power it from 3.3V. The address is 0x76 when SDO is to GND (0x77 otherwise).

projects.title: Barometer
projects.description: Print pressure, temperature and altitude.

projects.title: Weather station
projects.description: Combine with a DHT22 and show all readings on an LCD.

projects.title: Floor-level detector
projects.description: Detect which floor of a building you are on from the pressure change.

name: Pulse Sensor
purpose: Reads your heartbeat from a fingertip
summary: Optical heart-beat sensor that clips to a fingertip or earlobe and gives an analog pulse waveform.
tip: Cover the front with the clear sticker and don't press too hard. The PulseSensor Playground library calculates BPM for you.

projects.title: Heartbeat LED
projects.description: Blink an LED with each heartbeat.

projects.title: BPM display
projects.description: Show live BPM on an LCD.

projects.title: Stress biofeedback game
projects.description: A calming LED gets greener as your heart rate falls during deep breathing.

name: ECG Sensor AD8232
summary: Single-lead heart ECG front-end that outputs a clean analog ECG waveform.
tip: Use it with 3 ECG gel electrodes: red on the right chest, yellow on the left chest, green on the lower right abdomen. For safety, power the laptop from its battery, not the charger. This is not a medical device.

projects.title: ECG plot
projects.description: Plot your ECG waveform in the Serial Plotter.

projects.title: ECG heart-rate monitor
projects.description: Detect R-peaks and show BPM with lead-off warnings.

projects.title: Portable ECG recorder
projects.description: Record 30-second ECG clips to an SD card for viewing on a PC.

name: MAX6675 Thermocouple
summary: K-type thermocouple amplifier that measures 0–1024 °C in 0.25 °C steps. The probe is included.
tip: Read it no faster than every 250 ms or you'll get the same value. If the temperature falls when heated, swap the thermocouple wires.

projects.title: High-temp thermometer
projects.description: Read the temperature of a soldering iron tip.

projects.title: Over-temperature alarm
projects.description: Buzz when a heater passes a setpoint you choose with a rotary encoder.

projects.title: Reflow / kiln controller
projects.description: PID-control a heater through an SSR to follow a temperature profile.

name: APDS9960 Gesture Sensor
summary: Gesture, proximity, ambient light and RGB colour sensor in one chip.
tip: It is a 3.3V-only device. The 3.3V pin on clone Nanos is weak, so power it from an AMS1117-3.3 and use an I2C level shifter for reliable gestures.

projects.title: Proximity lamp
projects.description: Turn on an LED when your hand comes near.

projects.title: Colour reader
projects.description: Show the RGB value of objects on an RGB LED.

projects.title: Gesture-controlled home
projects.description: Swipe up/down for lights and left/right to move a servo blind.

name: Magnetic Reed Sensor
purpose: Knows if a door is open or closed
summary: Door/window reed switch with a magnet; the contact closes when the magnet is near.
tip: With INPUT_PULLUP the pin reads LOW when the door is closed and HIGH when it opens.

projects.title: Door alarm
projects.description: Beep when the door opens.

projects.title: Fridge door reminder
projects.description: Beep if the fridge door stays open for more than 30 seconds.

projects.title: Home security panel
projects.description: Monitor several doors, with keypad arming and an alarm log.

name: HX710 Air Pressure Sensor
purpose: Measures air pressure in a tube
summary: MPS20N0040D pressure sensor (0–40 kPa) with an HX710B 24-bit ADC, connected by a tube.
tip: Push a silicone tube onto the port. Calibrate the zero at open air first and then scale with a known level.

projects.title: Blow meter
projects.description: Show how hard you blow into the tube.

projects.title: Tank level by pressure
projects.description: A tube at the tank bottom measures water depth with no electronics in the water.

projects.title: Digital BP monitor model
projects.description: Inflate a cuff with a pump and detect pressure oscillations.

name: Water Flow Sensor (YF-S201)
summary: Hall-effect flow meter for 1–30 L/min that outputs pulses in proportion to the flow.
tip: Flow (L/min) ≈ pulse frequency (Hz) ÷ 7.5. Count pulses with attachInterrupt() on D2.

projects.title: Flow rate meter
projects.description: Print litres per minute every second.

projects.title: Water usage meter
projects.description: Show the total litres used on an LCD.

projects.title: Smart dispenser
projects.description: Dispense exactly 500 ml with a solenoid valve and stop automatically.

name: Metal Detector Module
summary: Standalone coil-based metal detector board with an onboard buzzer, which detects coins a few cm away.
tip: It works on its own with just power. Use the OUT pin, if your board has one, to read detections on the Nano.

projects.title: Coin finder
projects.description: Hide coins in sand and find them with the beeping detector.

projects.title: Metal-detecting robot
projects.description: A robot stops and flashes when it drives over metal.

projects.title: Metal detection logger
projects.description: Mark detection spots on a grid with a joystick and record them.

name: AC Voltage Sensor ZMPT101B
summary: Isolated mains voltage transformer module that outputs a small AC sine wave centred at 2.5V.
tip: DANGER: the input side is at mains voltage. Use screw terminals, an enclosure and supervision, and calibrate the trimmer against a multimeter. EmonLib calculates RMS for you.

projects.title: Mains present indicator
projects.description: Detect whether mains power is on (via the transformer module only).

projects.title: Voltage monitor
projects.description: Show RMS mains voltage on an LCD.

projects.title: Smart energy meter
projects.description: Measure V, A, W and kWh with a ZMPT101B and an ACS712.

name: 0–25V Voltage Sensor
summary: Simple 5:1 resistor divider that lets the Nano measure DC voltages up to 25V.
tip: Volts = analogRead(A0) × 5.0 / 1023 × 5. Never exceed 25V, and connect the source ground to the Nano ground.

projects.title: Battery checker
projects.description: Print the voltage of a 9V or 12V battery.

projects.title: Low-battery cut-off
projects.description: Disconnect the load through a relay when a 12V battery drops below 11.5V.

projects.title: Solar charge logger
projects.description: Log panel and battery voltage every minute to an SD card.

name: AC Current Sensor (ZMCT103C)
purpose: Measures the AC current an appliance uses
summary: Current-transformer module; pass a live wire through the hole to measure AC current up to 5A without cutting into the circuit.
tip: Pass only one conductor (live) through the core. Sample quickly and calculate RMS, or use EmonLib.

projects.title: Appliance on detector
projects.description: Light an LED when the kettle is drawing current.

projects.title: Appliance usage timer
projects.description: Log how many hours a fridge compressor runs each day.

projects.title: Motor overload protection
projects.description: Cut power to a motor through a relay when the current is too high.

name: ACS712 5A Current Sensor
summary: Hall-effect current sensor for ±5A AC or DC, with the current path isolated from the output.
tip: Output is 2.5V at 0A and changes by 185 mV per amp. Measure the zero offset at power-up, and average many samples because it is noisy. For AC, calculate RMS.

projects.title: DC current meter
projects.description: Measure the current of a small motor.

projects.title: Stall detector
projects.description: Detect a jammed motor from a current spike and stop it.

projects.title: Battery capacity tester
projects.description: Discharge a battery through a load and calculate mAh.

name: INA260 Power Monitor
purpose: Measures voltage, current and power precisely
summary: Precision I2C sensor with a built-in shunt that measures voltage (up to 36V), current (±15A) and power.
tip: Address 0x40 by default. Wire it on the high side, in series with the load positive.

projects.title: USB power meter
projects.description: Measure how much current your Nano project really uses.

projects.title: Battery discharge logger
projects.description: Record voltage, current and mAh during discharge.

projects.title: Solar MPPT experiment
projects.description: Sweep the panel load to find the maximum power point.

name: ACS712 20A Current Sensor
summary: Hall-effect current sensor for ±20A AC or DC.
tip: Output is 2.5V at 0A and changes by 100 mV per amp. Measure the zero offset at power-up, and average many samples because it is noisy. For AC, calculate RMS.

projects.title: Current meter
projects.description: Measure the DC current of a 12V device.

projects.title: Appliance power monitor
projects.description: Show the RMS current of an appliance on an LCD.

projects.title: Smart energy meter
projects.description: Combine with a ZMPT101B for V, A, W and kWh.

name: ACS712 30A Current Sensor
summary: Hall-effect current sensor for ±30A AC or DC, for higher-power loads.
tip: Output is 2.5V at 0A and changes by 66 mV per amp. Measure the zero offset at power-up, and average many samples because it is noisy. For AC, calculate RMS.

projects.title: High-current meter
projects.description: Measure the current of a 12V car accessory.

projects.title: Battery bank monitor
projects.description: Show charge and discharge current with direction arrows.

projects.title: Inverter load manager
projects.description: Shed non-critical loads by relay when the total current is too high.

name: Colour Sensor (TCS3200)
purpose: Tells the colour of an object
summary: RGB colour sensor that outputs a frequency for the red, green, blue or clear filter you select.
tip: Measure each filter with pulseIn(). Calibrate with white and black paper and map the readings to 0–255.

projects.title: Colour reader
projects.description: Print R, G and B values for objects you show it.

projects.title: Colour mimic lamp
projects.description: An RGB LED copies the colour of the object.

projects.title: Skittles colour sorter
projects.description: Two servos pick up candies and drop them into bins by colour.

name: Dust Sensor (GP2Y1010AU0F)
summary: Sharp optical dust sensor that detects fine particles (PM2.5-style dust density).
tip: Pulse the LED: set D7 LOW, wait 280 µs, read A0, then set it HIGH. Dust (mg/m³) ≈ 0.17 × V − 0.1. Add the 150Ω resistor and 220 µF capacitor.

projects.title: Dust reading
projects.description: Print the dust density every second.

projects.title: Air purifier controller
projects.description: Turn on a purifier fan when the dust level is high.

projects.title: Air quality logger
projects.description: Log dust, gas and climate data to SD as CSV.

name: Condenser Microphone
purpose: A small microphone that picks up sound
summary: Bare electret microphone capsule; it needs a bias resistor and an amplifier stage.
tip: On its own the signal is only a few millivolts. Use a transistor or LM358/MAX4466 amplifier biased at 2.5V before A0.

projects.title: Mic amplifier build
projects.description: Build a one-transistor amplifier and view the signal in the Serial Plotter.

projects.title: Sound-reactive LEDs
projects.description: LEDs flash to the beat of music.

projects.title: Clap-direction finder
projects.description: Two mics estimate which side a clap came from by timing difference.

name: IR LED + Photodiode Pair
purpose: Make your own infrared object sensor
summary: Matching IR emitter and receiver for building your own obstacle, beam-break or reflective sensors.
tip: The photodiode is reverse-biased. More IR means more current and a lower voltage at A0. Shield it from sunlight.

projects.title: DIY obstacle sensor
projects.description: Detect your hand by the change in analog reading.

projects.title: Beam-break counter
projects.description: Count objects passing between the facing LED and photodiode.

projects.title: DIY finger pulse sensor
projects.description: Shine IR through a fingertip and filter the signal to get BPM.

name: Photodiode (2 pcs)
summary: Fast light sensors that respond in microseconds, unlike slow LDRs.
tip: Reverse-bias it with a 10 kΩ–1 MΩ resistor: a bigger resistor is more sensitive but slower.

projects.title: Light flash detector
projects.description: Detect a phone camera flash.

projects.title: Strobe frequency meter
projects.description: Measure the flicker frequency of a lamp or LED.

projects.title: Li-Fi text receiver
projects.description: Receive text sent by a blinking LED on another Arduino.

name: Force Sensor Square (FSR406)
purpose: Measures how hard you press on a large pad
summary: Large square force-sensitive resistor (about 38 mm) whose resistance drops as you press harder.
tip: Use a 10 kΩ resistor from A0 to GND, with the FSR between 5V and A0. It shows relative force, not exact newtons or grams.

projects.title: Press meter
projects.description: Show press strength as an LED brightness.

projects.title: Chair occupancy sensor
projects.description: Track how long you sit and remind you to take breaks.

projects.title: Smart floor mat
projects.description: Count steps and detect a person standing at the door.

name: FSR 12.7 mm (FSR402)
summary: Round 12.7 mm force-sensitive resistor for fingertip-sized presses.
tip: Use a 10 kΩ resistor from A0 to GND, with the FSR between 5V and A0. It shows relative force, not exact newtons or grams.

projects.title: Squeeze meter
projects.description: Display squeeze force as a 5-LED bar.

projects.title: Finger drum pad
projects.description: Play different buzzer tones depending on how hard you hit.

projects.title: Robot gripper feedback
projects.description: Stop closing a servo gripper once a grip force is reached.

name: FSR 5.08 mm (FSR400)
purpose: Measures pressing force on a tiny spot
summary: Small 5 mm force-sensitive resistor for tiny buttons and fingertips.
tip: Use a 10 kΩ resistor from A0 to GND, with the FSR between 5V and A0. It shows relative force, not exact newtons or grams.

projects.title: Pressure button
projects.description: Light an LED only on a firm press.

projects.title: Typing pressure logger
projects.description: Measure how hard you press a key over time.

projects.title: Haptic glove fingertip
projects.description: Map fingertip pressure to vibration motor strength.

name: Flex Sensor 2.2 inch
purpose: Measures how much it is bent
summary: Bend sensor whose resistance rises from about 25 kΩ flat to about 100 kΩ bent.
tip: Use a 47 kΩ resistor divider. Bend it in one direction only, and protect the base (where the leads join) from flexing.

projects.title: Bend meter
projects.description: Print the bend angle by mapping the flat and fully-bent readings.

projects.title: Finger-controlled servo
projects.description: Bending your finger moves a servo.

projects.title: Robotic hand glove
projects.description: Five flex sensors drive five servos in a robotic hand.

name: 10K Thermistor
purpose: A cheap part that senses temperature
summary: NTC thermistor (10 kΩ at 25 °C, β ≈ 3950) whose resistance falls as it gets hotter.
tip: Convert with the Beta equation: 1/T = 1/298.15 + ln(R/10000)/3950, with T in kelvin.

projects.title: Thermometer
projects.description: Calculate and print °C with the Beta equation.

projects.title: Fridge temperature alarm
projects.description: Beep if the fridge is warmer than 8 °C for 10 minutes.

projects.title: Thermostat with hysteresis
projects.description: Control a heater with an adjustable setpoint and a 1 °C band.

name: LM35 Temperature Sensor
summary: Analog sensor that outputs 10 mV per °C; no library needed.
tip: °C = analogRead(A0) × 500 / 1023. Swapping +Vs and GND makes it hot, so check the pinout with the flat face towards you.

projects.title: Serial thermometer
projects.description: Plot temperature in the Serial Plotter.

projects.title: Temperature-controlled fan
projects.description: Fan speed rises with temperature using PWM.

projects.title: Multi-room temperature panel
projects.description: Read three LM35s and show min/max of each on an LCD.

name: DS18B20 Waterproof
purpose: Measures the temperature of water and liquids
summary: Digital temperature probe (−55–125 °C, ±0.5 °C) in a waterproof steel tube.
tip: It needs a 4.7 kΩ pull-up. Many probes can share one pin because each has a unique address.

projects.title: Water thermometer
projects.description: Print water temperature in °C.

projects.title: Aquarium heater control
projects.description: Keep the tank at 26 °C through a relay-controlled heater.

projects.title: Multi-probe solar heater logger
projects.description: Log inlet, outlet and tank temperatures to SD.

name: DS18B20 Module
summary: DS18B20 digital temperature sensor on a module with the pull-up resistor and LED onboard.
tip: The pull-up is already on the module. Use DallasTemperature to read °C with 9–12 bit resolution.

projects.title: Room thermometer
projects.description: Print temperature every second.

projects.title: Overheat cut-off
projects.description: Disconnect a device through a relay above 60 °C.

projects.title: Temperature data logger
projects.description: Log readings with timestamps and draw a graph on the PC.

name: 5 mm LDR
summary: Bare light-dependent resistor whose resistance falls in brighter light.
tip: With the LDR on top and 10 kΩ to GND, the reading rises as it gets brighter.

projects.title: Light meter
projects.description: Print a 0–100 % light level.

projects.title: Fading night light
projects.description: An LED fades in smoothly as the room gets darker.

projects.title: Light-seeking robot
projects.description: Two LDRs steer a robot toward the brightest light.

name: 12 mm LDR
purpose: Senses light level, works better in dim light
summary: Larger LDR that is more sensitive in low light than the 5 mm version.
tip: Larger area means better low-light response. Use 4 of them for a two-axis solar tracker.

projects.title: Dusk detector
projects.description: Turn on an LED at dusk, with hysteresis so it doesn't flicker.

projects.title: Single-axis solar tracker
projects.description: Two LDRs and a servo turn a small panel toward the sun.

projects.title: Dual-axis solar tracker
projects.description: Four LDRs and two servos track the sun across the sky.

name: TSOP1738
summary: Bare 38 kHz IR receiver IC for TV-remote signals.
tip: The TSOP1738 pinout is GND–Vs–OUT, different from the TSOP1838 (OUT–GND–Vs). Check the datasheet for your part.

projects.title: Remote key printer
projects.description: Print any remote's key codes.

projects.title: IR-controlled fan speed
projects.description: Use remote keys to set fan speed with PWM.

projects.title: IR object counter
projects.description: A 38 kHz IR LED and TSOP form a long-range beam-break counter.

name: TSOP1738 Metal Cap
purpose: Receives remote signals, works well near motors
summary: TSOP1738 IR receiver with a metal shield that rejects electrical noise.
tip: The shield helps near motors and switching supplies. Add 100Ω in series with Vs and a 4.7 µF capacitor to GND for extra stability.

projects.title: Remote key printer
projects.description: Print any remote's key codes.

projects.title: Remote relay board
projects.description: Control four relays with a TV remote.

projects.title: IR robot control
projects.description: Drive a motorised robot without the motor noise causing glitches.

name: 5 kg Load Cell
summary: Aluminium bar strain-gauge load cell for weights up to 5 kg.
tip: Connect it to an HX711: red E+, black E−, white A−, green A+. Mount it so only the arrow end is loaded, then calibrate with a known weight.

projects.title: Raw weight reading
projects.description: Print raw HX711 values while pressing the bar.

projects.title: Digital kitchen scale
projects.description: Weigh in grams on an LCD, with a tare button.

projects.title: Smart pill/stock shelf
projects.description: Count identical items by weight and alert when stock is low.

name: 10 kg Load Cell
summary: Bar load cell for up to 10 kg, for heavier scales.
tip: Connect it to an HX711: red E+, black E−, white A−, green A+. Mount it so only the arrow end is loaded, then calibrate with a known weight.

projects.title: Weight printer
projects.description: Print weight in kg after calibration.

projects.title: Pet food bowl monitor
projects.description: Track how much your pet eats each day.

projects.title: Beehive scale logger
projects.description: Log hive weight daily to track honey production.

name: 50 kg Load Cell
purpose: Weighs people, like a bathroom scale
summary: Half-bridge body-scale load cell (3 wires). Use four of them to make a full bathroom-scale bridge.
tip: One cell is only half a bridge. Use 4 cells with a combiner board, or 1 cell plus 2 × 1 kΩ resistors, before the HX711.

projects.title: Half-bridge test
projects.description: Wire one cell with two resistors and see the reading change when pressed.

projects.title: Bathroom scale
projects.description: Four cells under a board make a body-weight scale.

projects.title: Bed occupancy monitor
projects.description: Detect when someone gets out of bed at night for elderly care.

name: 35 mm Piezo Plate
summary: Piezo disc that works as a knock sensor (it generates a voltage) or as a buzzer.
tip: As a sensor, put a 1 MΩ resistor across it and read A0. It can produce voltage spikes, so add a 5.1V Zener for protection. As a buzzer, drive it with tone().

projects.title: Knock detector
projects.description: Light an LED when the table is knocked.

projects.title: Electronic drum pad
projects.description: Play a sound whose loudness follows hit strength.

projects.title: Secret knock lock
projects.description: Record a knock rhythm and open a servo latch when it matches.

name: 27 mm Piezo Plate
summary: Smaller piezo disc for knock sensing or making sound.
tip: As a sensor, put a 1 MΩ resistor across it and read A0. It can produce voltage spikes, so add a 5.1V Zener for protection. As a buzzer, drive it with tone().

projects.title: Piezo melody
projects.description: Play a tune with tone().

projects.title: Tap counter
projects.description: Count taps on a table and show the number on LEDs.

projects.title: Footstep energy demo
projects.description: Rectify the piezo output to charge a capacitor and light an LED.

name: Hall Effect Sensor Module
summary: Linear Hall-effect sensor with a comparator that detects magnets and magnetic field strength.
tip: AO sits at about 2.5V and moves up or down depending on the magnet's pole. Adjust the trimmer for the DO threshold.

projects.title: Magnet detector
projects.description: Light an LED when a magnet is near.

projects.title: Bicycle speedometer
projects.description: A wheel magnet triggers the sensor and you calculate km/h.

projects.title: Contactless liquid level
projects.description: A float magnet triggers sensors at different heights in a tube.

name: AS608 Fingerprint Sensor
summary: Optical fingerprint module that stores up to about 160 fingerprints and does the matching itself.
tip: The AS608 runs on 3.3V (the R307 runs on 5V). Wire colours vary, so check your cable. Enroll fingers with the Adafruit 'enroll' example first, at 57600 baud.

projects.title: Fingerprint enroll & match
projects.description: Enroll your finger and print the matched ID.

projects.title: Fingerprint door lock
projects.description: Open a solenoid lock for enrolled fingers, with lockout after 3 failures.

projects.title: Attendance system
projects.description: Log the finger ID with date and time to SD.

name: 1-Channel Touch
summary: Single TTP223 capacitive touch button on a round pad.
tip: The output goes HIGH while touched. You can stick it behind up to about 3 mm of plastic.

projects.title: Touch LED
projects.description: LED on while touching.

projects.title: Touch toggle switch
projects.description: A touch toggles a relay.

projects.title: Touch piano key
projects.description: Combine several pads into a mini piano with a buzzer.

name: 4-Channel Touch (TTP224)
summary: Four capacitive touch keys on one board, each with its own output pin.
tip: Each output is HIGH while its key is touched.

projects.title: Four-key LEDs
projects.description: Each key lights its own LED.

projects.title: Touch relay panel
projects.description: Four keys toggle four relays.

projects.title: Touch PIN lock
projects.description: Enter a 4-digit PIN with the touch keys to open a servo lock.

name: 8-Channel Touch
summary: Eight capacitive touch keys with parallel outputs.
tip: It uses 8 pins. If you're short of pins, read the outputs through a 74HC165 shift register.

projects.title: Touch keyboard test
projects.description: Print which key is touched.

projects.title: Touch piano
projects.description: Play 8 notes of a scale on a buzzer.

projects.title: Touch MIDI controller
projects.description: Send MIDI notes over USB serial to music software on a PC.

name: PWM Touch Dimmer
purpose: Turns lights on and dims them by touch
summary: Touch dimmer board: a tap toggles the output and a long press sets the brightness via PWM.
tip: It works on its own for LED dimming. To read the brightness on the Nano, measure the duty cycle with pulseIn().

projects.title: Touch-dim LED
projects.description: Dim an LED by touch without any code.

projects.title: Brightness reader
projects.description: Read the dimmer's duty cycle and show it as %.

projects.title: Touch-dim LED strip
projects.description: Drive a 12V strip through a MOSFET and sync a second strip from the Nano.

name: E18-D80NK IR Proximity
purpose: Detects objects up to 80 cm away
summary: Adjustable 3–80 cm industrial IR proximity sensor in a threaded barrel.
tip: The NPN output goes LOW when an object is detected. Set the range with the screw on the back.

projects.title: Object detector
projects.description: Light an LED when something is in range.

projects.title: Automatic hand dryer model
projects.description: Run a fan while hands are under the sensor.

projects.title: Conveyor counting & rejection
projects.description: Count items and push out every 10th one with a servo for inspection.

name: MQ2 Sensor (bare)
summary: Bare MQ2 gas element for smoke and LPG, for building your own module or PCB.
tip: The bare sensor needs a circuit: heater pins (H) to 5V/GND, A pins to 5V, and B pins to A0 with a 10 kΩ load resistor to GND. The heater draws about 150 mA.

projects.title: Build the circuit
projects.description: Wire the load resistor and read smoke levels on A0.

projects.title: Smoke alarm PCB
projects.description: Solder your own smoke alarm board with buzzer.

projects.title: Rs/R0 ppm estimate
projects.description: Calculate Rs/R0 and estimate ppm from the datasheet curve.

name: MQ3 Sensor (bare)
summary: Bare MQ3 alcohol gas element.
tip: The MQ3 datasheet recommends a 200 kΩ load resistor. Let it warm up for at least 2 minutes before reading.

projects.title: Alcohol sniffer
projects.description: Show the alcohol level on a 5-LED bar.

projects.title: Wine fermentation tracker
projects.description: Watch alcohol vapour rise over days.

projects.title: Calibrated breath meter
projects.description: Estimate mg/L with the datasheet curve (demo only).

name: MQ6 Sensor (bare)
summary: Bare MQ6 element for LPG, butane and propane.
tip: The bare sensor needs a circuit: heater pins (H) to 5V/GND, A pins to 5V, and B pins to A0 with a 20 kΩ load resistor to GND. The heater draws about 150 mA.

projects.title: LPG reading
projects.description: Read the LPG level and print it.

projects.title: Cylinder leak alarm
projects.description: A loud buzzer and LED for LPG leaks.

projects.title: Leak alarm with auto-valve
projects.description: Close a solenoid valve on a leak until reset.

name: RCWL-0516 Microwave Radar
summary: Doppler microwave motion sensor that sees movement up to about 7 m, even through plastic or thin walls.
tip: OUT goes HIGH (3.3V, which the Nano reads fine) for about 2 seconds on motion. Keep it away from metal and fans, which cause false triggers.

projects.title: Motion LED
projects.description: Light an LED when anything moves.

projects.title: Hidden porch light
projects.description: A light turns on behind a plastic cover when someone approaches.

projects.title: Dual-tech intruder alarm
projects.description: Combine with a PIR so the alarm sounds only when both detect motion.
